title: No Gun Ri massacre
summary: Between 26 and 29 July 1950, early in the Korean War, US soldiers of the 7th Cavalry Regiment killed South Korean refugees near No Gun Ri, firing on them as they sheltered under a railroad bridge. The toll is disputed. After a 1999 press investigation the US Army review of 2001 called it a tragedy, not deliberate killing; survivors and Korean investigators disagree.

where.modern_name: Nogeun-ri (No Gun Ri), Yeongdong County, North Chungcheong Province, South Korea
where.historical_name: No Gun Ri, Hwanggan Myon, Yongdong Gun, North Chungchong Province, Republic of Korea

importance.justification: One of the best-documented killings of civilians by US forces in the Korean War and a long-running dispute over responsibility and compensation.

audience_note: Describes the killing of civilians, mostly women, children and older people. Death toll, intent and orders are disputed.

sources.title: The No Gun Ri Massacre: When American Soldiers Killed Hundreds of South Korean Refugees
Survivors of the No Gun Ri Incident
Statement by Secretary of Defense William Cohen on the No Gun Ri review, 11 January 2001

reviewer_note: Casualty figures are attributed in the record, not in the summary: South Korea certified 163 dead or missing and 55 wounded in 2005 (Military.com); the No Gun Ri Peace Foundation estimates 250-300 killed; survivors estimate about 400; the US Army says the number is unknown. Orders are disputed: the Army found no evidence of orders to shoot; South Korean investigators cited veterans who believed such orders existed. Dates 26-29 July are on two opened pages. Not opened: Wikipedia, AP articles.
